conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-01.question: In Exodus 3:12, God promises Moses that an angel would be with him.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-01.learningObjective: Observe that God promises Moses his own presence.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-01.feedbackCorrect: God sends no one in his place: he himself says "Certamente estarei contigo".

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Exodus 3:12: God himself promises "Certamente estarei contigo" (I will surely be with you).

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-01.hint: See who is speaking and whom he is speaking about.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-02.question: In Exodus 3:11, tap the king Moses would have to go to.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-02.learningObjective: Identify before whom Moses would be sent.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-02.feedbackCorrect: Pharaoh was the king of Egypt, the most powerful man Moses would have to face.

feedbackWrong.a: Moses is speaking with God; the king he would have to face is someone else.
feedbackWrong.b: Egypt is the country, not the king.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-02.hint: Look for a king's title right after "ir até" (go to).

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-03.question: According to Exodus 3:12, what would be the sign that God sent Moses?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-03.learningObjective: Observe the sign God gives Moses.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-03.feedbackCorrect: The sign would come later: freed from Egypt, the people would serve God on that mountain.

feedbackWrong.b: The text does not promise leaving that same day; the sign comes after the exodus.
feedbackWrong.c: The verse does not speak of Moses' courage; it speaks of the people serving God.
feedbackWrong.d: The bush is not the sign here; the sign is the people on the mountain.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-03.hint: Read what comes after "este será o sinal" (this will be the sign).

options.a: The people, already free, would serve God on that mountain
options.b: Pharaoh would let the people go that same day
options.c: Moses would speak without fear before the king
options.d: The bush would keep burning for years

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-04.question: Put Exodus 3:16 in the order of the text.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-04.feedbackCorrect: First the order to gather the elders, then who appeared, and then what God saw.

feedbackWrong.default: The verse begins with the command to Moses; what God saw in Egypt comes at the end.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-04.hint: The verse begins with a command to Moses.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-05.question: In Exodus 3:13, what does Moses imagine the people will ask about God?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-05.learningObjective: Remember the question that leads to the revelation of the name.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-05.feedbackCorrect: The people would want the name of the one who sent Moses, to know who he is.

feedbackWrong.a: Moses does not imagine questions about plans; he imagines questions about who God is.
feedbackWrong.b: The question Moses imagines is not about strength; it is about what God is called.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-05.hint: See the question the people would ask, near the end of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-06.question: What does Exodus 3:14 communicate that connects to this context?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-06.learningObjective: Connect the revealed name to Moses' mission.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-06.feedbackCorrect: God gives Moses the name he will carry: "EU SOU me enviou a vocês".

feedbackWrong.a: Moses does not go on his own; he goes in the name of the one who sends him.
feedbackWrong.c: Pharaoh does not send Moses; God is the one who sends.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-06.hint: See what Moses must say to the children of Israel.

options.a: Moses goes in his own name
options.b: God names the one who sends him

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-01.question: In Exodus 3:11–12, God answers Moses' doubt by praising his qualities.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-01.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between Moses' doubt and God's answer.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-01.feedbackCorrect: God does not talk about Moses' qualities: he answers with his own presence.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Exodus 3:12: God's answer is "Certamente estarei contigo", not praise.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-01.hint: Compare Moses' question with the first sentence of the answer.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-02.question: In Exodus 3:10, tap the words that mark the purpose of Moses' sending.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-02.learningObjective: Recognize the purpose marker in Moses' call.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-02.feedbackCorrect: "Para que" (so that) opens the purpose: Moses goes to free God's people from Egypt.

feedbackWrong.a: "Vem agora" (come now) is the call; the purpose comes after.
feedbackWrong.b: "Do Egito" (from Egypt) says where the people would leave; the purpose link comes before.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-02.hint: Look for the link in the middle of the verse, after "Faraó".

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-03.question: In Exodus 3:14–15, how does the name "EU SOU" (I AM) relate to the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-03.learningObjective: Relate the revealed name to God's history with Israel.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-03.feedbackCorrect: Right after "EU SOU", God presents himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

feedbackWrong.a: God says this is his name forever, from generation to generation.
feedbackWrong.c: The next verse ties the name to Israel's fathers: it is not another God.
feedbackWrong.d: God tells Moses to take the name to the children of Israel; it is no secret.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-03.hint: See how God presents himself right after saying the name.

options.a: It is a title that holds only while the people are in Egypt
options.b: It is the same God who already cared for Israel's fathers
options.c: It is a new God, who replaces the God of their ancestors
options.d: It is a secret name, for Moses alone to know

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-04.question: How does the conversation move forward in Exodus 3:11–12?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement of the conversation between Moses and God.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-04.feedbackCorrect: Moses looks at himself; God answers with his presence and a sign still to come.

feedbackWrong.default: The conversation begins with Moses' doubt; the sign is the last thing God says.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-04.hint: Who speaks first in this dialogue?

options.c: God gives a sign still to come

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-05.question: In Exodus 3:12, what does God promise Moses in answer to his doubt?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-05.learningObjective: Understand that God's presence is the answer to Moses' doubt.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-05.feedbackCorrect: God promises to be with him: his presence answers Moses' "Quem sou eu?".

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not say God would go in his place; it says he would be with him.
feedbackWrong.b: God does not promise to speak for Moses here; he promises to be with him.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-05.hint: It is the first sentence of God's answer.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-06.question: What links Exodus 3:15 to Psalm 9:10?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-06.learningObjective: Relate the revealed name to the trust of God's people.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-06.feedbackCorrect: God gives his name to be known, and those who know him learn to trust him.

feedbackWrong.b: The name holds from generation to generation: the same God for all of them.
feedbackWrong.c: God has the name taken to the people, and the psalm speaks of those who know it.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-06.hint: See what the psalm says about those who know God's name.

options.a: Those who know the name trust

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-01.question: In Exodus 3:14, Moses' authority before the people comes from the one who sends him, not from himself.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-01.learningObjective: Interpret Moses' mission as resting on who God is.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-01.feedbackCorrect: Moses shows no credentials of his own: he says that "EU SOU" (I AM) sent him.

feedbackWrong.false: Moses must say "EU SOU me enviou a vocês": the weight is on the one who sends.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-01.hint: See what Moses must say to the people.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-02.question: In Exodus 3:15, tap the word that shows this name of God has no expiry date.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that God's name holds forever.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-02.feedbackCorrect: God does not present himself only for that moment: the name is forever.

feedbackWrong.a: "Assim" (thus) introduces what Moses must say, not how long the name holds.
feedbackWrong.b: "Ainda mais" (further) only shows that God keeps speaking.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-02.hint: Look right after "este é o meu nome" (this is my name).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-03.question: What reading does Exodus 3:13–14 support about God's name?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about God's name.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-03.feedbackCorrect: God answers the question and even tells Moses to take the name to the children of Israel.

feedbackWrong.a: Moses speaks of the "Deus de seus pais": "EU SOU" is that same God.
feedbackWrong.b: God answers "EU SOU O QUE SOU" and sends the name to the people: there is no refusal.
feedbackWrong.c: The weight is not on Moses: "EU SOU me enviou a vocês".

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-03.hint: See what God tells Moses to do with the name.

options.a: I AM is a new god, different from the God of the fathers
options.b: God refuses to tell Moses his name
options.c: The mission depends on Moses being strong and prepared
options.d: God makes himself known and has his name taken to the people

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-04.question: Which sequence shows the promise of Exodus 3:12 being fulfilled?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-04.learningObjective: See in Exodus 3:12 a promise that God keeps.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-04.feedbackCorrect: God promises, frees the people, and brings them to the same mountain: he keeps his word.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: promise (Exod 3:12), leaving Egypt (Exod 12:51), and the mountain (Exod 19:2).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-04.hint: The promise comes first; the mountain is the arrival point.

options.a: God promises the people will serve him on that mountain
options.b: God brings the children of Israel out of Egypt
options.c: Israel camps in front of the mountain of God

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-05.question: In Exodus 3:15, how does God say he wants to be kept from generation to generation?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows God's name passed between generations.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-05.feedbackCorrect: The name is meant to be remembered: each generation knows God by it.

feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of fear here; it speaks of memory passed on.
feedbackWrong.c: Worshiping God is good, but the verse speaks of remembering the name.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-05.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-06.question: What links Exodus 3:14 to John 8:58?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-06.learningObjective: Connect the name revealed at the bush to Jesus' words, as the NT does.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus says "before Abraham was, I AM": he takes the name from the bush for himself.

feedbackWrong.b: Jesus does not say "I was" but "I AM": he speaks of who he is, before Abraham.
feedbackWrong.c: Neither text says that; the point is who says "I AM".

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-06.hint: Compare Jesus' last words with the name given to Moses.

options.a: Jesus uses the same "EU SOU" (I AM)
options.b: Jesus speaks only of his age

estudo:entrada-deus-02.context: Moses had fled Egypt and lived in the desert tending sheep. From the bush that burned without burning up, God calls him to bring Israel out of slavery. Moses hesitates and asks what to say when the people want to know who sent him.
estudo:entrada-deus-02.focusQuestion: Moses asked "who am I?" and God answered by saying who he is. Where do you need to look more at God than at yourself?
estudo:entrada-deus-02.keywordGloss: The name God reveals to Moses: he is who he is, depends on no one, and is with his people.
facts: Moses asks who he is to go to Pharaoh.
God promises to be with Moses.
Moses asks what name he will tell the people.
God answers: I AM WHO I AM.
God presents himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God says this is his name forever.
